## [QuickBooks Desktop → QuickBooks Online\ Migration](https://www.upwork.com/jobs/QuickBooks-Desktop-QuickBooks-Online-Migration_~022092041501885760494/?referrer_url_path=/nx/search/jobs/)

- **Fixed price**
- **Expert**
- **Est. budget:** **$5,000.00**

Overview
We're looking for an experienced accountant or bookkeeper to migrate a client's QuickBooks Desktop
company file to QuickBooks Online. This is not a “run the Intuit migration tool and hope for the best”
job. We need someone who has done real QBD→QBO conversions, knows where they break, and can
make deliberate decisions about what carries over and what gets rebuilt.
This is a fixed-price engagement at $5,000 USD. It is not hourly, and we are not looking for hourly bids.
The budget is set — what we're evaluating is whether you can deliver the scope below for it.
The engagement has two distinct phases.
Phase 1 — Trial Balance Migration
Establish the opening balances in QBO as of an agreed cutover date. This includes:
• Building or mapping the QBO chart of accounts (a clean account structure, not a 1:1 dump of legacy
accounts)
• Posting the trial balance as of the conversion date via journal entry
• Migrating open A/R and A/P detail so aging reports are accurate — not just a lump balance
• Reconciling bank, credit card, and clearing accounts to the Desktop file
• Carrying over customer, vendor, and item/product-service lists with sensible naming
• Confirming inventory and COGS balances tie to the source file
• Delivering a signed-off reconciliation showing QBO balances agree to QBD as of the cutover date
Phase 2 — Transactional Detail and Scrubbing (closer to present day)
For the more recent periods, we need actual transactional detail in QBO, not just summary balances.
Expect hands-on cleanup work:
• Importing or re-entering transactions for the recent period(s)
• Identifying and correcting mis-coded, duplicated, or orphaned transactions before they land in QBO
• Normalizing customer/vendor/item naming so downstream reporting and integrations work
• Re-reconciling affected periods after the scrub
This phase is done in tandem with the Luminous team. Luminous is the client's inventory and order
management platform, and it syncs data into QuickBooks. Some of the transactional detail originates on
our side, and decisions about how transactions should be structured in QBO (item mapping, GL account
mapping, how inventory and COGS post) need to be made jointly. You'll be on working sessions with our
team, comparing records, agreeing on treatment, and validating results together. We're not handing you
a file and disappearing — but we do need someone who can drive the accounting decisions and tell us
when we're wrong.

Scope and Price
fixed price, covering:
• Full trial balance conversion as of the cutover date, reconciled and signed off
• Open A/R and A/P detail migration
• Chart of accounts, customer, vendor, and item list setup in QBO
• Transactional detail for \[DATE RANGE — e.g. the trailing 6 months\], including scrubbing and
correction
• Up to \[N\] joint working sessions with the Luminous team
• Reconciliation of affected periods and a final tie-out package
Milestones will be structured in Upwork as \[e.g. 40% on Phase 1 sign-off / 60% on final tie-out\] — happy
to discuss the split.
Out of scope (would be a separate agreement): historical transactional detail beyond the period above,
ongoing bookkeeping after cutover, payroll conversion, multi-entity consolidation, and remediation of
accounting errors that existed in the Desktop file before we started. If you hit something material that
falls outside this, we want to hear about it early — not at the end.

Requirements — please read before applying
We explicitly want someone who has performed QuickBooks Desktop to QuickBooks Online
migrations before. This is a hard requirement, not a preference. If this would be your first one, this isn’t
the right job for you and we will not be a good training ground. In your proposal, tell us how many
QBD→QBO conversions you have personally completed and describe at least one in detail.
Also required:
• Strong working knowledge of both QuickBooks Desktop and QuickBooks Online, including where
QBO cannot replicate QBD behavior
• Comfort building and posting trial balance conversion entries, and reconciling them to the source
file
• Experience migrating open A/R and A/P detail (not just balances)
• Experience with inventory-carrying businesses and how inventory/COGS convert
• Ability to work through imports at volume (IIF/CSV, Transaction Pro, SaasAnt, Dancing Numbers, or
similar) and to explain which tool you’d use and why
• Clear written communication and availability for live working sessions with our team during \[YOUR\
TIME ZONE / OVERLAP HOURS\]
• Discretion with confidential financial data

• Experience migrating a QuickBooks file connected to an external inventory/OMS/ERP system
• QuickBooks ProAdvisor certification (Online and/or Desktop)
• Familiarity with QBO’s API or third-party sync tools and how they post transaction

o Apply, Please Answer
1\. How many QBD→QBO migrations have you personally completed? Describe the most complex one
— file size, what broke, and how you handled it.
2\. How do you decide what to bring over as full transactional detail versus opening balances only?
3\. What’s your approach to migrating open A/R and A/P so aging reports stay accurate?
4\. What tools do you use for bulk transaction import, and why that one?
Have you migrated a QuickBooks file that was integrated with an inventory or order management
system? What did you have to watch out for?
6\. Based on the scope above, what would you need to see before you’re comfortable committing to
$5,000 fixed?
Proposals that don’t answer these questions will not be reviewed. Please skip the generic cover letter —
we’d rather read three specific paragraphs about a migration you actually did.
